title: CSL SBA G10 2026 GUIDELINES TO SCHOOLS

COMMUNITY SERVICE LEARNING
SCHOOL BASED ASSESSMENT
Grade 10
2026
PROJECT
INSTRUCTIONS TO SCHOOLS
 1. The 2026 CSL Project will be carried out as per the guidelines provided.
 2. Learners should be guided to observe safety while undertaking the tasks.
 3. Core competencies and values embedded in the project tasks will be assessed.
 4. Each learner is required to develop and maintain an assessment portfolio as evidence
 of achievement. The entries in the portfolio should include:
 i. Evidence of the learner’s work on each of the tasks.
 ii. Teachers’ comments on the learner’s work as the project continues.
 iii. Learner’s own reflection on the project work.
 iv. Dates when each of the tasks is undertaken, and when the assessment is done.
 5. Group tasks should be submitted for scoring after each project implementation step and
 evidence kept in the group assessment portfolio.
 6. The assessment portfolio may be physical, electronic (e-portfolio) or both.
 7. Each school is to set out a calendar for assessment of the tasks within the provided
 timelines.
 8. Items required for the assessment must be assembled before the set dates.
 9. The teacher will use the scoring guide provided to assess the learner’s project work.
 10. Scoring and uploading learners’ scores should be completed by 31st October 2026.

1.0 TARGETED SUBJECT GENERAL LEARNING OUTCOMES
By the end of Senior School, the learner should be able to:
 a) Engage in community initiatives at all levels as a responsible citizen,
 b) Respect and value diversity for peaceful coexistence,
 c) Apply life and financial skills to create sustainable social enterprises,
 d) Use research skills to improve self and community,
 e) Uphold integrity, care for others, and promote positive values,
 f) Communicate effectively and build cross-cultural relationships,
 g) Recognize the impact of Community Service Learning on societal issues.
2.0 ASSESSMENT STANDARDS
By the end of Senior School, the learner can:
 a) Participate responsibly and actively in community initiatives to address identified community
 needs.
 b) Demonstrate respect for diverse cultures, beliefs, and perspectives in interactions and
 community activities.
 c) Apply life and financial management skills to develop and sustain a social enterprise that
 addresses a community need.
 d) Use appropriate research methods to investigate issues and propose evidence-based solutions
 for self and community improvement.
 e) Demonstrate integrity, empathy, and positive values in decision-making and community
 engagement.
 f) Communicate effectively and collaborates with people from diverse cultural backgrounds to
 achieve shared goals.
 g) Evaluate and reflect on the contribution of Community Service Learning activities to
 addressing societal issues
3.0 TARGETED STRANDS AND SUB-STRANDS
 STRANDS SUB-STRANDS
 Citizenship 1.1 Concepts of Community Service Learning
 1.2 Community Needs
 1.3 Leadership Development
 1.4 Intercultural Competence
 Life Skills in 2.1 Self-Awareness in the Community
 Education 2.2 Conflict Resolution
 Action Research 3.1 Introduction to Action Research
 3.2 Problem Identification
4.0 VALUES TO BE DEVELOPED
 a) Respect- as the learners take turns during discussions at steps one through three, in
 Task 1, and consider the guidance from their leaders and CSL teachers.
 b) Unity- as the learners display teamwork in assigned roles for the completion of the
 project. All eight steps require teamwork.
 c) Integrity- As the learners adhere to the project guidelines, select leadership and use
 the resources responsibly across all the tasks.
5.0 TARGETED CORE COMPETENCIES
 a) Communication and collaboration- as the learners discuss, brainstorm, consult and
 engage one another at different stages in all three tasks.
 b) Critical thinking and problem-solving- as the learners identify community need(s) in
 Task one related to the theme of the project.
 c) Self-efficacy- as the learners perform different tasks, come up with journals and do
 presentations, particularly in steps seven and eight.
 d) Citizenship (leadership)- as the learners select group leaders, define their roles and
 plan for implementation in task one, and execute project activities in task two.
 e) Digital Literacy- as the learners search for relevant information during tasks
 execution.
6.0 TARGETED PERTINENT AND CONTEMPORARY ISSUES
 a) Social cohesion- as learners display mutual coexistence in groups with diversity
 during the project period.
 b) Good governance: as learners adapt their group leadership for different roles in the
 project activities.
 c) Civic Responsibility- as learners explore and use locally available resources in tasks
 one and two for their project work.
7.0 EXPECTED IMPACT OF THE PROJECT
 a) Improved learner empathy and appreciation of diversity
 b) Practical understanding of inclusivity and cohesion
 c) Enhanced learner agency and responsible citizenship
8.0 PROJECT TASK
PROJECT THEME
BUILDING INCLUSIVITY AND SOCIAL COHESION IN OUR COMMUNITY
Social problems within the school community undermine learners’ well-being, hinder
effective learning and strain healthy relationships.
In groups of 6-8 and with guidance from the teacher, learners will:
 i. Identify a social problem within the school community related to the theme.
 ii. Design an intervention plan or solution to address the social problem.
 iii. Develop an action plan for implementing the project (timelines, milestones, resources,
 etc)
 iv. Implement the action plan accordingly.
 v. Reflect on the project (preparation, implementation and the post-implementation
 stage).
 vi. Write a reflective report and make a presentation of the project to the class/school
 community.
vii. Present the project report.
TASK 1
8.1 TEACHER GUIDELINES FOR TASK 1: PREPARATION STAGE
 a) Form inclusive groups of 6-8 learners and assign each group a unique code/number for
 coordination.
 b) Clarify the theme, purpose, context, scope of the project and the expected outputs to
 the learners.
 c) Guide the learners to identify and define the challenge, gap or problem in the
 community in relation to the theme provided.
 d) Develop a simple action plan (what, where, how, who, etc.)
 e) Guide learners to link classroom learning (subjects and strands) with the present
 community project activities.
 f) Guide learners to seize the opportunity to develop relevant values and core
 competencies as they execute different tasks.
 g) Provide guidelines on safety measures to be observed as they undertake the project.
 h) Brainstorm with learners on general expectations and conduct as they go about the
 project.
 i) Brief learners on modes of assessment that will be employed in the project work.
 j) Guide learners to explore cost-effective or locally available resources in their projects.
 k) Guide learners to identify, define roles, contact and document relevant partners within
 the school for their project.
 l) Guide learners on ethical and inclusive considerations while undertaking the project,
 including, but not limited to:
 i. Respect for other persons and community members,
 ii. No discrimination or stigmatisation,
 iii. Confidentiality where necessary,
 iv. No duplication or replication of people's work.
 m) Familiarise with the Grade 10 CSL Curriculum Design and the provided project
 assessment scoring guide.
 n) Guide learners in selecting realistic and relevant problems/gaps/focus areas for the
 project.
 o) Participate in peer consultations with other teachers, particularly those handling the
 same subject for the same cohort.
 p) Reinforce the point that how learners relate to each other is as important as the
 completion of the community service project itself.
 q) Encourage learners to design and implement different group projects and avoid
 duplication.
 r) Guide learners to identify the targeted beneficiary for their project and how it will
 benefit them.
 s) Guide learners to develop a simple action plan (what, where, how, who, etc.).
 t) Guide learners to journal or document their meetings and forums where decisions
 about their projects are made.
8.2 LEARNERS' INSTRUCTIONS FOR TASK 1
8.2.1 Step 1: Group leadership formation and comprehending the project
 a) Select group leadership and define the roles and responsibilities for all.
 b) Brainstorm the instructions provided and appreciate the task at hand.
8.2.2 Step 2: Identify a school community problem related to the project theme
 a) Discuss and list several problems, challenges or gaps that you have observed or
 experienced in your school community.
 Note: Some pointers to your school community's problems/gaps may include
 checking who feels left out, what situations cause division, disharmony or conflict,
 and what has affected togetherness in the school community.
 b) Brainstorm the problems in a) and adopt one of them for your CSL project. Give
 reasons for your selection.
 c) Write down 2-3 paragraphs describing the nature and extent of the problem selected.
8.2.3 Step 3: Design an intervention or solution to deal with the problem
 a) Search for possible solutions to the identified problem in Step 2.
 b) Brainstorm in your groups on potential solutions. Consider what you will do, what
 you will require, who the beneficiaries of your project are, and where the project will
 be undertaken.
 c) Confirm that the solution relates to the project theme, is realistic, ethical and
 appropriate to the school context.
 d) Brainstorm how the solution can be implemented, linking it to previous class work in
 school.
 e) Approach relevant members of the school community or stakeholders to validate the
 project choice. Revise accordingly.
 f) Finally, discuss and design a title for the project.
8.2.4 Step 4: Project Planning and Organisation
 Work together as a group to create a detailed plan that you will use to implement the
 solution in Step 3. Complete the implementation matrix attached.
 a) Determine and outline key activities to be undertaken to implement the solution.
 b) Identify appropriate and locally available materials or resources to be used in project
 implementation.
 c) Come up with milestones(stages) and timelines for checking the project progress.
 d) Develop rules to ensure punctuality, respect, safety and active participation.
 e) Identify responsibilities for each group member, as well as
 persons/partners/stakeholders who can be part of your project. Give reasons for the
 selection.
NOTE: Outputs for Task 1-Learners to have the following in their group portfolio:
 • Group roles defined and names of group members.
 • Project identified and noted down (discussion notes)
 • Agreed intervention designed (discussion notes)
 • Project Implementation matrix completed
 • Reflection notes on task 1.
TASK 2
8.3 TEACHER GUIDELINES FOR TASK 2: IMPLEMENTATION STAGE
From the implementation matrix completed in task 1, guide learners to execute the activities.
Guide them to record progress in their portfolio for each activity undertaken and reflect in
their notes.
 a) Monitor compliance with the ethical and safety measures, including observing
 school rules and regulations as they perform project tasks.
 b) Encourage teamwork and responsibility- ensuring all group members are
 involved
 c) Offer guidance only when needed. Require learners to troubleshoot within
 their groups before seeking teacher support.
 d) Use the scoring guide as provided to assess the project progress.
 e) Monitor progress in the development of core competencies and values
 f) Guide learners to document their activities either through journals, notes,
 photographs, videos or artefacts (where appropriate) and file in their
 portfolios.
 g) Address any arising conflicts constructively, modelling empathy and
 respectful dialogue.
 h) Guide them to facilitate group reflective sessions to check on progress.
8.4 LEARNERS' INSTRUCTIONS TASK 2
8.4.1 Step 5: Carry out the project activities
 a) Implement your planned activities
 b) Be respectful, responsible, and inclusive
 c) Cooperate and support one another
 d) Work together with relevant community members
 e) Conduct reflective group discussions as the implementation progresses.
For example: conduct awareness sessions, organise inclusive school activities, promote
kindness through posters or drama, support a vulnerable group, etc.
8.4.2 Step 6: Documentation of the project progress
 While working:
 a) Take notes of each of the activities undertaken.
 b) Note down challenges and successes.
 c) Collect evidence (photos/videos/sketch notes, etc.)
 d) Prepare a summary of the group reflection on the progress of the project.
 e) Maintain an individual portfolio comprising the outputs.
NOTE: Outputs for task 2
 • Completed project implementation activities in the project implementation matrix.
 • Evidence of activities carried out, like notes, photos, journal entries, videos, etc
 • Individual learner portfolio up to date with learner reflections.
TASK 3
8.5 TEACHER GUIDELINES FOR TASK 3: POST-IMPLEMENTATION STAGE
 a) Guide learners to have reflective activities addressing what was done, what subjects
 were applied, benefits, changes in attitudes or perspectives, and record their varied
 reflections in portfolios, creative expressions. Encourage reflections on lessons
 learned.
 b) Support groups to prepare and present their project outcomes (encourage use of digital
 devices) in classes/school.
 c) Encourage sharing of learners' recommendations with the school community. One or
 more members should attend the presentation of the projects undertaken.
 d) Encourage learners to appreciate CSL as a continuous cohesive effort, not a one-off
 activity.
 e) Assess learners using the provided CSL assessment tools and provide constructive
 feedback to the learners.
 f) Record learners’ scores on the provided score sheet, then upload the final scores to the
 KNEC Portal within the set timelines.
8.6 LEARNERS' INSTRUCTIONS TASK 3
8.6.1 Step 7: Reflecting on the project
 a) As a group, discuss and note down:
 i.What worked well?
 ii.What challenges did you face?
 iii.How would you address such challenges in future projects?
 iv.How does your project benefit the entire school community?
 b) Each learner should reflect and complete their portfolio, giving examples:
 i. What did I learn?
 ii. How did this project change my thinking?
 iii. What went well?
 iv. What was challenging?
 v. What will I improve next time?
 vi. What was my contribution?
 vii. What values did I develop?
 viii. What skills or competencies did I gain?
 ix. Which subjects did I relate the project with, and how does the project connect to
 my classroom learning?
 (Use the attached template for individual Learner Reflection.)
8.6.2 Step 8: Report writing and presentation
 a) Write a group report using the following outline:
 i. The title of the project
 ii. A brief description of the problem
 iii. The solution implemented
 iv. Key project activities carried out
 v. Challenges and lessons learnt
 vi. Conclusion and recommendations
 b) Prepare and present the project report (use of digital devices is encouraged) in the
 classroom/school.
 c) Invite one or more school community members to attend the presentation and provide
 feedback.
 d) Creatively involve all the group members in the presentation.
 (Use the attached template for report writing.)
 NOTE: Outputs for Task 3
 • Completed project tasks and the report
 • Completed Implementation matrix
 • Evidence of group presentation in class/school
 • Evidence of group reflections on the project accomplished
 • Evidence of individual learner reflections on the project accomplished
 • Group report
